# FPL Points Lab

> Predicted Fantasy Premier League points for every player, from a gradient boosting model trained on
> four seasons of Premier League match data. Retrained and republished after each gameweek.

Season 2026-27, predictions for gameweek 11 (using games through gameweek 10).
Data source: official FPL API. Last refreshed: 2026-11-11.

## Pages

- [Home](https://andrewkwon0804-web.github.io/fpl-analyzer/): this week's best XI, last gameweek's result, track record and findings
- [Dashboard](https://andrewkwon0804-web.github.io/fpl-analyzer/dashboard.html): every player's prediction, player lookup, model team, transfer planner and analysis
- [Model report](https://andrewkwon0804-web.github.io/fpl-analyzer/research.html): accuracy on a held-out season against simple baselines, calibration, error analysis, feature importance, leakage check and an in-browser SQL lab
- [Raw predictions (JSON)](https://andrewkwon0804-web.github.io/fpl-analyzer/data/site.json): everything the site shows, in one file
- [Source code and method](https://github.com/andrewkwon0804-web/fpl-analyzer#readme): Python, SQL (SQLite) and scikit-learn pipeline

## Method in short

Features are rolling averages of points, minutes, xG and xA plus opponent strength, built in SQL with every
window ending at 1 PRECEDING so no row sees its own match. The model was tuned on 2024-25 and tested on
2025-26, a season left out of training; over that season its best XI scored 261 more
points than a team picked by season average. Predictions are multiplied by FPL's chance of playing.
